title: Measure of a collision piece
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $k \ge 1$. Fix two distinct elements $x \ne y$ of $\alpha$ and a value $a \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, and equip the space of hash functions $\alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ with the product of the uniform probability measures on the coordinates. Then the collision piece consisting of those hash functions $h$ with $h(x) = a$ and $h(y) = a$ has measure
\[
  \left(\frac{1}{k}\right)^2.
\]
replaced:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $k \ge 1$, $x \ne y \in \alpha$, and $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$.
Under the product measure on $\texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k$,
\[
  \mu_{\mathbb{R}}(\texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a) = \left(\frac{1}{k}\right)^2.
\]
